THE GATE READS THIS FILE FROM THE BASE TREE, NEVER FROM THE BRANCH. That is the entire
security model: a branch cannot self-authorize, because the entry that exempts its edit
must already be on main — i.e. it arrived through a PR a human reviewed. Two-PR
discipline, enforced mechanically (Myk, 2026-07-26): first land the authorization here,
An entry exempts a frozen-rail edit ONLY when base + the applicable substitutions is
byte-identical to the branch's file (directly, or after the repo's own prettier). Any
edit beyond the declared substitution is a violation, same as ever.
Shape: { from, to, files?, authorized }. `files` limits the pair to exact paths; an
UNSCOPED pair applies to every frozen rail and must be word-shaped (identifier or quoted
literal) — a SCOPED pair may carry wider literals (a regex fragment, a title phrase)
because the reviewer reads it against the named files. `authorized` names who and when.
Remove entries once the rename that consumed them has merged; a spent entry is inert
(the substitution no longer produces the base) but tidiness keeps this file reviewable.

renames.//: T136 rail REPAIR. The (1) single-use test builds its wrong verifier as verifier.replace(/.$/, "A"). A 32-byte verifier is 43 base64url chars whose LAST char carries only 4 bits, so ~6% already end in "A" (measured 12357/200000 = 6.18%) — the substitution then changes nothing, the wrong verifier IS the right one, redemption correctly answers 200, and the rail fails. On those runs the PKCE-mismatch path is never exercised. The replacement mutates to a char that cannot equal the original: 0 of 200000 unchanged. EXPRESSION ONLY — the first attempt tried to add explanatory comments in the same pair and was correctly refused as malformed, because the guard caps a pair at one line of 120 printable chars.
renames.from: verifier.replace(/.$/, "A")
renames.to: verifier.slice(0, -1) + (verifier.endsWith("A") ? "B" : "A")
renames.authorized: Myk, 2026-08-05 — repair a PKCE fixture whose mutation sometimes did not mutate; authorized in chat, re-shaped to one line after the guard refused the first pair

renames.//: T159 rail REPAIR — one pair across 19 frozen rails. vitest.config.mjs sets testTimeout: 20_000 and its comment says why: real sqlite fsync and WAL cycles legitimately cost seconds on a loaded windows runner. 32 test files then set 15000 and pull themselves BELOW that default; 19 of them are frozen. None of the 32 sets hookTimeout, so every one of them already runs its HOOKS at 20s while capping its TESTS at 15s — the line is a copied habit, not a considered budget. The 32 breach in turn, so the flake picks a different file each week: archive.test.ts measured 20.1s against its own 15s ceiling with #359's Defender exclusion applied, and even on a healthy main run its slowest test burned 11098ms of the 15000 (2026-08-11, Actions run 31522995407); path-resolution.test.ts timed out at 15s on PR #363. THIS RAISES NO BUDGET ABOVE THE DEFAULT. It stops 19 frozen rails from asking for less room than the repo already grants every other test file. Myk authorized this exact pair once before, for archive.test.ts alone (#356, merged); the edit was closed at #357 pending a root cause; that root cause landed as T155 and #359; and the pair then left this file unconsumed in #358, on the stated belief that 15s now carried real headroom. The 11098ms is what falsified that belief. No assertion moves in any of the 19 files — the only bytes that change are the digits in the budget.

renames.to: vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 20_000 });

renames.//: T139 rail REPAIR. render-sandbox.test.ts:103 asserts a 1ms budget times out even a TRIVIAL bundle, to prove renderTimeoutMs genuinely reaches the worker. That was only ever true because worker SPAWN sat inside the budget: T139 split the clocks (a legitimate spec-accuracy fix -- spawn latency measured the host, not the bundle, and 500ms of it turned a healthy render into a false 500 under load), so a trivial render now finishes inside 1ms and the assertion's premise is gone. The rail's INTENT survives and the fixture does not. This pair points it at the 'hang' route the same fixture already publishes (an infinite loop, line 42), which can only ever end at the clock -- so the knob is still proven to reach the worker. The sharper property the old spelling accidentally carried, that the OPERATOR'S number governs rather than some default, moves to T139's own unfrozen render-spawn-clock.test.ts with a bounded-duration bundle that distinguishes 1ms from 10s. No assertion changes: it still demands 500 and 'the renderer timed out'.
